knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r}
library(RcmdrShiny)
```

# Overview

The Report Studio is the **Report** tab in Studio mode. It authors R Markdown
and knitr documents while sharing the document buffer with the Script tab. The
lifecycle is **template or blank -> edit -> preview -> run cells -> knit ->
download**.

The fast preview never executes code; the knit executes every chunk in the
session.

# Templates

```{r}
names(RcmdrShiny:::report_templates())
```

A template is a function of the data set name and the title. It only uses
commands that the dialogs already generate.

```{r}
text <- RcmdrShiny:::report_template_text("profile", "Dataset", "Data profile")
cat(head(text, 12), sep = "\n")
```

# Documents

The registry keeps every open document while `state$document` remains the
active buffer for backward compatibility.

```{r}
state <- AppState()
RcmdrShiny:::document_registry_ensure(state)
RcmdrShiny:::document_create(state, "rmd", "Example", text = "## Section")
RcmdrShiny:::document_list(state)
```

The outline and the chunk list are pure functions of the text.

```{r}
doc <- RcmdrShiny:::document_text(state)
RcmdrShiny:::document_outline(doc, "rmd")
```

# Preview

`report_preview()` renders Markdown with `commonmark` and replaces chunks with
labelled placeholders. It does not run code.

```{r}
preview <- RcmdrShiny:::report_preview(
  c("## Results", "", "```{r}", "summary(Dataset)", "```"), "rmd"
)
class(preview$html)
```

# Executable cells

A cell run goes through `run_command()` and is stored under
`state$cell_outputs`; the document is not modified.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::report_run_cell(state, "chunk-01", doc, "rmd")
RcmdrShiny:::report_cell_status(state, "chunk-01")
```

# Insertion

Insertion is explicit and never happens on preview or on a cell run.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::report_insert_output(state, history_id)
RcmdrShiny:::report_insert_plot(state, plot_id, caption = "Figure 1")
RcmdrShiny:::report_insert_data_profile(state, "Dataset")
RcmdrShiny:::report_insert_model_summary(state, "LinearModel.1")
```

# YAML front matter

The form merges fields instead of replacing the block, so unknown metadata is
preserved.

```{r}
header <- c("---", 'title: "Old"', "custom: keep", "---", "", "Body")
tmp <- AppState()
RcmdrShiny:::document_create(tmp, "rmd", "Meta", text = header)
RcmdrShiny:::document_set_front_matter(tmp, list(title = "New", toc = TRUE))
cat(RcmdrShiny:::document_text(tmp))
```

# Knit

`document_knit()` renders the document in the session environment and records
the attempt in `state$knit_history`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
result <- RcmdrShiny:::document_knit(state, "html")
result$file
```

Formats explain why they are unavailable:

```{r}
RcmdrShiny:::document_format_reason("pdf", "rmd")
```

# Autosave

```{r, eval = FALSE}
RcmdrShiny:::document_autosave(state)
RcmdrShiny:::document_recoveries(state)
```

# Design notes

- The preview and the knit are clearly separate: one does not execute code,
  the other does.
- Cell output is session state; the knit is the final source of truth.
- YAML round-trips conservatively.
- Templates never add a statistical procedure.
- Classic mode keeps the historical Report iframe.
